description: Pull out quotes with premiums above £1,500 for review.
Keep web and phone quotes for drivers aged 25 to 70 whose premium is missing or at least £250.
Find priced quotes in the AB and XY postcode areas with a plausible postcode format.
Calculate the premium per £1,000 insured and a monthly instalment including a five percent charge.
Cap vehicle values for rating and measure the absolute gap between vehicle value and sum insured.
Create natural-log and base-ten severity measures for positive, non-declined claims.
Route quotes to decline, referral, missing-price review or acceptance using ordered underwriting rules.
Give claim-free drivers an NCD discount that depends on their years earned and sales channel.
Standardise postcode capitalisation and trim and lowercase the categorical rating fields.
Extract the outward code, inward code and postcode length for a geography quality check.
Build a readable rating segment key and remove whitespace from postcodes.
code: df = quotes.with_columns(pl.concat_str([pl.col('region'), pl.col('channel'), pl.col('fuel')], separator='|').alias('segment_key'), pl.col('postcode').str.replace_all(r'\s+', '').alias('compact_postcode'), pl.col('channel').str.replace('phone', 'telephone', literal=True).alias('channel_label'))

description: Add inception year, month, day and weekday for seasonality analysis.
Calculate the next annual renewal date and the end of a 14-day cooling-off period.
Measure the age of each 2025 claim at the end of that year.
code:
df = claims.filter((pl.col('claim_date') >= pl.date(2025, 1, 1)) & (pl.col('claim_date') < pl.date(2026, 1, 1)))
df = df.with_columns((pl.date(2025, 12, 31) - pl.col('claim_date')).dt.total_days().alias('claim_age_days'))

description: Prepare string policy identifiers, integer premium pence and a fixed set of fuel categories for export.
Parse the numeric district from the postcode and leave unparseable districts missing.
Create a quote extract without policy identifiers, postcodes or vehicle values and give premium a clearer name.
Summarise every floating-point quote measure without listing the measures individually.
Order quotes by region and descending premium with missing prices last and quote ID as the tie-breaker.
code: df = quotes.sort(['region', 'premium', 'quote_id'], descending=[False, True, False], nulls_last=True)

description: Keep the quote with the latest inception date for each policy, breaking ties with the highest quote ID.
code:
df = quotes.sort(['policy_id', 'start_date', 'quote_id'])
df = df.unique(subset=['policy_id'], keep='last', maintain_order=True).sort('policy_id')

description: Exclude every quote belonging to a repeated policy and inception-date combination.
Compare quote volume, priced volume, distinct policies and premium totals by region and channel.
Compare median, upper-tail and variability measures of claim severity across claim statuses.
Calculate open and closed claim amounts and count large non-declined claims for each policy.
Attach the regional mean, regional channel median and descending regional premium rank to every quote.
Number each policy's claims chronologically and calculate its running claim amount.
Compare each quote with the preceding quote for the same policy in inception-date order.
Attach the regional rate and factor to every quote and calculate their product as a benchmark.
code:
df = quotes.join(rates, on='region', how='left', validate='m:1', maintain_order='left')
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('base_rate') * pl.col('factor')).alias('regional_benchmark'))

description: Find quotes on policies with no open or closed claims.
Keep quotes on policies with at least one open claim of £10,000 or more without multiplying quote rows.
code:
large_open_claims = claims.filter((pl.col('status') == 'open') & (pl.col('amount') >= 10000))
df = quotes.join(large_open_claims, on='policy_id', how='semi').sort('quote_id')

description: Compare each priced quote with the mean premium for its region and channel.
code:
benchmarks = quotes.drop_nulls('premium').group_by(['region', 'channel']).agg(pl.col('premium').mean())
df = quotes.drop_nulls('premium').join(benchmarks, on=['region', 'channel'], how='inner', suffix='_benchmark', validate='m:1')
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('premium') - pl.col('premium_benchmark')).alias('premium_gap')).sort('quote_id')

description: Show the benchmark premium for each quote under every available regional rate scenario.
code:
scenarios = rates.rename({'region': 'scenario_region'})
df = quotes.select('quote_id', 'region', 'premium').join(scenarios, how='cross')
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('base_rate') * pl.col('factor')).round(2).alias('scenario_premium')).sort(['quote_id', 'scenario_region'])

description: Combine missing-price and high-price quotes into one queue with an explicit review reason.
code:
missing_prices = quotes.filter(pl.col('premium').is_null()).with_columns(pl.lit('missing_price').alias('review_reason'))
high_prices = quotes.filter(pl.col('premium') > 2000).with_columns(pl.lit('high_price').alias('review_reason'))
df = pl.concat([missing_prices, high_prices], how='vertical').sort(['review_reason', 'quote_id'])

description: Combine quote inceptions and claims into a policy timeline while retaining their different financial fields.
code:
quote_events = quotes.select('policy_id', pl.col('quote_id').alias('record_id'), pl.col('start_date').alias('event_date'), 'premium', pl.lit('quote').alias('event_type'))
claim_events = claims.select('policy_id', pl.col('claim_id').alias('record_id'), pl.col('claim_date').alias('event_date'), 'amount', 'status', pl.lit('claim').alias('event_type'))
df = pl.concat([quote_events, claim_events], how='diagonal').sort(['policy_id', 'event_date', 'event_type', 'record_id'])

description: Require complete rating identifiers and replace missing premiums with zero in a reporting-only column.
Fill a missing quote premium from the preceding known premium on the same policy.
Fill missing premiums from the regional median, then the portfolio median, then an explicit £500 default.
Put average web, broker and phone premiums into separate columns for each region.
code: df = quotes.pivot(on='channel', on_columns=['web', 'broker', 'phone'], index='region', values='premium', aggregate_function='mean').sort('region')

description: Turn premium, sum insured and vehicle value into a long table of quote financial measures.
List the three largest non-declined claims for each policy, using claim ID to break equal-amount ties.
code:
df = claims.filter(pl.col('status') != 'declined').sort(['policy_id', 'amount', 'claim_id'], descending=[False, True, False], nulls_last=True)
df = df.group_by('policy_id').agg(pl.col('claim_id').head(3).alias('largest_claim_ids'))
df = df.explode('largest_claim_ids').rename({'largest_claim_ids': 'claim_id'}).join(claims, on=['policy_id', 'claim_id'], how='inner').sort(['policy_id', 'amount', 'claim_id'], descending=[False, True, False], nulls_last=True)

description: Assign vehicle-value bands with explicit cut points and age bands with ordered underwriting thresholds.
Calculate each channel's share of quotes within its region and across the whole portfolio.
Apply regional factors to positive quoted premiums and summarise the financial impact by region and movement band.
code:
df = quotes.filter(pl.col('premium') > 0)
df = df.join(rates, on='region', how='inner', validate='m:1')
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('premium') * pl.col('factor')).round(2).alias('proposed_premium'))
df = df.with_columns(pl.when(pl.col('proposed_premium') < pl.col('premium')).then(pl.lit('decrease')).when(pl.col('proposed_premium') <= pl.col('premium') * 1.10).then(pl.lit('zero_to_ten_percent')).otherwise(pl.lit('over_ten_percent')).alias('movement_band'))
df = df.group_by(['region', 'movement_band']).agg(pl.len().alias('quote_count'), pl.col('premium').sum().alias('current_premium_total'), pl.col('proposed_premium').sum().alias('proposed_premium_total'))
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('proposed_premium_total') - pl.col('current_premium_total')).alias('premium_change'), (pl.col('current_premium_total') / pl.col('current_premium_total').sum()).alias('current_premium_share'))
df = df.sort(['region', 'movement_band'])

description: Attach each quote's non-declined claim history from the three calendar years before inception and flag repeat claimants.
code:
accepted_claims = claims.filter(pl.col('status').is_in(['open', 'closed']))
history = quotes.select('quote_id', 'policy_id', 'start_date').join(accepted_claims, on='policy_id', how='inner').filter((pl.col('claim_date') >= pl.col('start_date').dt.offset_by('-3y')) & (pl.col('claim_date') < pl.col('start_date')))
history = history.group_by('quote_id').agg(pl.len().alias('prior_claim_count'), pl.col('amount').sum().alias('prior_claim_amount'), pl.col('claim_date').max().alias('latest_prior_claim_date'))
df = quotes.join(history, on='quote_id', how='left', validate='m:1')
df = df.with_columns(pl.col('prior_claim_count').fill_null(0), pl.col('prior_claim_amount').fill_null(0.0))
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('prior_claim_count') >= 2).alias('repeat_claimant'), (pl.col('start_date') - pl.col('latest_prior_claim_date')).dt.total_days().alias('days_since_last_claim'))
df = df.select('quote_id', 'policy_id', 'premium', 'prior_claim_count', 'prior_claim_amount', 'repeat_claimant', 'days_since_last_claim')
df = df.sort('quote_id')

description: Find up to three latest priced quotes per region with the largest proportional premium excess over their regional age-band median.
code:
df = quotes.sort(['policy_id', 'start_date', 'quote_id']).unique(subset=['policy_id'], keep='last', maintain_order=True)
df = df.filter(pl.col('premium') > 0)
df = df.with_columns(pl.when(pl.col('age') < 25).then(pl.lit('under_25')).when(pl.col('age') < 65).then(pl.lit('25_to_64')).otherwise(pl.lit('65_plus')).alias('age_band'))
df = df.with_columns(pl.col('premium').median().over(['region', 'age_band']).alias('peer_median'))
df = df.with_columns((pl.col('premium') / pl.col('peer_median') - 1).alias('premium_excess')).filter(pl.col('premium_excess') > 0)
df = df.sort(['region', 'premium_excess', 'quote_id'], descending=[False, True, False])
df = df.with_columns(pl.int_range(1, pl.len() + 1).over('region').alias('review_position'))
df = df.filter(pl.col('review_position') <= 3).select('region', 'review_position', 'quote_id', 'policy_id', 'age_band', 'premium', 'peer_median', 'premium_excess').sort(['region', 'review_position'])
